newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen slow on lack of domestic news.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen slow on lack of domestic news.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to stagnate in early trade on Monday on the lack of fresh domestic leads, brokers said.
But a sharp rise on Wall Street on Friday could prompt some fresh buying in firstliners and in counters included in the new Morgan Stanley Capital Index (MSCI), they added.
On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average soared nearly 95 points on news of a plan to balance the federal budget.
However, brokers said, local market sentiment was likely to stay cautious as the campaign for the May 29 general election continues.
"Maybe the market will be active again after the general election, with first quarter results driving trading," one local broker said.

Brokers said news reports that four companies might be delisted from the Jakarta bourse due to their inability to book profits for three consecutive years is likely to prompt some selling in the counters.
The four companies named in newspapers include PT Pan Brothers Tex, PT Great Golden Star, PT Pool Asuransi and PT Langgeng Makmur Plastic Industry.
On Friday, the Jakarta index fell 2.56 points to close at 647.89 points after touching a low of 644.53 points.
Advancers led decliners 77 to 58 with 73 issues unchanged. Turn-over by midsession was 115 billion rupiah.
Telkom, the largest capitalised stock on the market, rose 50 rupiah to 3,500 rupiah, with around one million shares traded, brokers said.
"I don't see any new major fundamental changes affecting Telkom, the rise was largely due to bargain-hunting as Telkom had fallen below the 3,500 rupiah level recently," another broker said.
Brokers said reports that the Busang gold deposit in Kalimantan was a hoax had weakened sentiment on Timah.
Timah fell 125 rupiah to 3,800 rupiah, with some 450,000 shares traded.

"It was lucky for Timah not to get involed in the Busang project despite its previous efforts to do so, but players were cautious on the firm's gold exploration efforts after the Busang fraud reports," one broker said.
Indonesian partners in the Busang field are not listed.
The most actively traded Bank BNI rebounded 25 rupiah to 1,475 rupiah, with some 4.6 million shares traded.
Small chemical firm Duta Pertiwi rose 500 rupiah to 2,325 rupiah, with some 7.5 million shares traded, on market talk of a possible rights issue, brokers said.
